I will score each idea on those axes rather than on prose quality.

READ: B spec text ("USE_BEHAVIOUR ... Behaviour off sets all c_p = 1"; "lambda_p(x) = 2/(1 - c_p ||x||^2)") against B evidence E12 ("c_p = -kappa_p in (0.1, 10.0)") and E13 (acts inside quantizer at every level, in assignment score and residual recursion).

With latents bounded by tanh (||x|| -> 1) the denominator 1 - c_p||x||^2 goes to 1 - 1*1 = 0 in the control branch, so lambda diverges.
REASONING: A control that changes the sign convention and sits on a pole is not a matched control: it differs from the shipped arm in more than the intended switch. On the rubric this caps falsifiability at 2 ("controls that differ in more than the intended switch") and is a genuine numerical hazard for implementability (B names "deeper levels could become numerically stiff" but specifies no guard/clamp). OPEN: Whether this alone is decisive, or whether behavioural/downstream evidence also favours A.`;

const rec3 = `GOAL: Score behavior_evidence and downstream_mechanism for both ideas against the shared measured rows.
READ: A hypothesis ("Spearman |A_k| vs B_k clearly positive ... H(next code | level-0 code) will fall ... test Recall@10 above 0.065") vs B hypothesis ("higher per-level code entropy concentrated in the top fanout quartile ... higher training prefix-conditional next-code accuracy"). Shared E5 (successor entropy H 0.931 -> 3.405 across quintiles, support 2.8 -> 44.3, top-1 mass 0.4375 -> 0.0543, Spearman -0.973) and E8 (pair co-membership K=16 0.3106, K=32 0.2164, K=64 0.1547, K=256 0.0822).
OBSERVED: A names the exact assignment change (argmin and commitment at every residual level, per-code cell size s[l][k]) and two observables with an expected direction plus a stated failure statistic (Spearman |A_k| vs B_k ~ 0). E5 does support the premise that branching varies hugely, which is the strongest shared asset, and A exploits it at the cell level where the quantizer actually decides.
OPEN: Novelty/exploration comparison against the E6 negative ledger.`;

READ: E6 recall@10 for the whole family: l1_br 0.04671, successor_entropy 0.05122, successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, successor_geodesic_coarse_v2 0.05463, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500, versus l1_br_euclid 0.06207, l1_only 0.06233, resample 0.06363. Also E7 per-position NLL for the same runs.

READ: All of the above: A bundle e9e97242e0e9ed08 (E5, E8, E12, E13, spec, hypothesis) and B bundle 404ea254563870a6 (E5, E6, E8, E12, E13, spec switches).
OBSERVED: A is stronger on falsifiability (two genuinely nested off-switches - unit-curvature collapse and curvature removal preserving behaviour weights - plus a stated falsifier in Spearman |A_k| vs B_k and a named discriminating diagnostic), on downstream_mechanism (named assignment change at argmin and commitment, named observable H(next code | level-0 code), named direction and threshold 0.065), on novelty/exploration (self-consistent partition-curvature fixed point is not in the E6 ledger), and on implementability (explicit clamp, no gradient into s, cumulative-mean refresh, 12 scheduled refreshes, quantified +2-4% budget). B is stronger on raw cost (<1%) but that dimension is 10% and A's cost is already negligible.
REASONING: B loses on three counts that are each independently disqualifying at the top of the rubric: its behaviour-off control flips the c_p sign convention of its own E12 (c_p=-kappa_p) to c_p=+1 and therefore sits on the lambda pole; its geometric operation is a per-node scalar residual multiply that a matched Euclidean scalar reproduces; and its premise of finer resolution for hub prefixes is contradicted by E8 (K=16 0.3106 vs K=256 0.0822) and sits in the E6 family of four measured negatives. A wins.
FAILURE RISK: A's own listed risk is the live one - the encoder can absorb the field so that Spearman |A_k| vs B_k stays near zero; and the broader family evidence (successor_entropy 0.05122, geodesic_coarse 0.05500) plus E8's coarse-beats-fine result mean the curvature-budget premise may simply be wrong, in which case A lands at or below l1_only 0.06233 rather than above 0.065. Additionally the rescaled distance is not a metric, so cells can empty or become non-convex and the fixed point can drift to a few huge low-curvature cells.
ANSWER: WINNER CURVCELL-SID; FIRST LISTED CURVCELL-SID (A was printed first in the prompt).`;

await tools.progress.append_progress({content: rec5});
return "ok";
